content:
Each tile has area \(4\), and the \(5\times4\) board has area \(20\), so at most \(5\) tiles could fit.

Color the board like a chessboard. A \(5\times4\) board has \(10\) black and \(10\) white squares. Every T-shaped tile covers \(3\) squares of one color and \(1\) of the other, so its contribution to the black-white difference is \(\pm 2\). Five such tiles would give a total difference that is a sum of five numbers each equal to \(\pm2\), which cannot be \(0\). Thus \(5\) tiles cannot cover the whole board. Hence at most \(4\) can be placed.

Four tiles can indeed be placed, for example:
\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
A&A&A&B&\cdot\\
D&A&B&B&\cdot\\
D&D&C&B&\cdot\\
D&C&C&C&\cdot
\end{array}
\]
where each letter marks one T-shaped tile and the last column is empty.

Therefore, the maximum number is
\[
\boxed{4}
\]
